skill.name: qa
skill.description: Run an interactive QA session that turns user-reported bugs into focused GitHub issues. The skill clarifies reports, explores project context, and writes durable issue descriptions.
skill.summary: Turns conversational QA reports into clear, user-focused GitHub issues.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: I confirmed one real risk: the skill tells the agent to create GitHub issues with `gh issue create` without user review. The other static findings are Markdown issue templates inside code fences, not executable commands. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation of the issue title and body before running `gh issue create`.
State that the GitHub CLI must be authenticated and scoped to the intended repository before filing issues.

static_findings.snippet: Create issues with `gh issue create`. Do NOT ask the user to review first — just file and share URLs

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 49 explicitly instructs the agent to create GitHub issues with `gh issue create` without user review. This is an external command with repository side effects, even though it matches the skill purpose.
Lines 57-75 are a fenced Markdown template for an issue body. They contain placeholders and headings, not executable shell syntax.
Lines 75-83 are Markdown fence boundaries and nearby prose about issue ordering. They do not contain a command invocation or command interpolation.
Lines 83-109 are a fenced Markdown template for multi-issue reports. The content is issue text with placeholders, not executable code.

content.value_statement: Bug reports often miss clear reproduction steps and user impact. This skill turns QA conversations into focused GitHub issues with concise context.
actual_capabilities: Guides short clarification questions for bug reports.
Explores repository context to use accurate product language.
Decides whether one report should become one issue or several issues.
Drafts concise GitHub issue bodies with expected behavior and reproduction steps.
Uses GitHub CLI issue creation when the environment allows it.
limitations: It requires GitHub CLI access to file issues automatically.
It does not diagnose root causes or implement fixes.
It depends on the user for accurate reproduction details.
It may expose sensitive report details if issues are filed without review.

use_cases.title: Triage User-Reported Bugs
use_cases.description: Convert a support conversation into a focused GitHub issue with expected behavior and reproduction steps.

use_cases.title: Run Manual QA Sessions
use_cases.description: Capture defects found during exploratory testing and split broad reports into actionable issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare Developer Backlogs
use_cases.description: Create durable issues that describe user-facing behavior without stale file paths or internal implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Start a QA Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a QA session for this repository. I will describe one bug, and you should ask only essential clarifying questions.

prompt_templates.title: File One Clear Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn this report into one GitHub issue: [describe what happened, what you expected, and any steps you know].

prompt_templates.title: Break Down a Broad Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this QA report and decide whether it should become several issues. Create separate issues only for independently fixable behaviors.

prompt_templates.title: Use Project Language
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore the repository context, then write GitHub issues using the project domain language. Avoid file paths, line numbers, and implementation details.

output_examples.input: The checkout page accepts an expired coupon but then fails at payment.
output_examples.output: A GitHub issue describing the checkout behavior, expected coupon rejection, reproduction steps, and payment impact.

output_examples.input: The import flow has validation errors, missing progress feedback, and a confusing success state.
output_examples.output: Several focused issues ordered by dependency, each with a clear scope, expected behavior, and testing notes.

output_examples.input: A user says the sync failed, but they do not know which action caused it.
output_examples.output: A short clarification request for reproduction details before filing, followed by a concise issue when enough evidence exists.

best_practices: Confirm sensitive details before filing issues in public repositories.
Provide exact steps, expected behavior, and actual behavior when possible.
Keep each filed issue focused on one user-facing behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to file issues without repository permission.
Do not include secrets, customer data, or private logs in issue bodies.
Do not ask it to diagnose or fix the bug during the QA session.

faq.question: Does this skill fix bugs?
faq.answer: No. It captures QA reports and files GitHub issues. It does not implement code changes.

faq.question: Does it need GitHub CLI access?
faq.answer: Yes, automatic filing requires `gh issue create` with access to the target repository.

faq.question: Can it create multiple issues from one report?
faq.answer: Yes. It splits reports when problems are independently fixable or have separate symptoms.

faq.question: Will it include file paths or line numbers?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent to describe user-facing behavior instead of internal implementation details.

faq.question: Is it suitable for public repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but review sensitive details before filing because issue bodies may become public.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
